minutes.headline: Assessors approved the FY2025 tax recap, rejected a public-notice motion, and promised to seek a state fix for an 86% condo error.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors went through the principal assessor's status report: the state-approved FY2025 tax rate, a line-by-line check of the commitment against State Form 54, exemption counts, a billing-system bridge problem, and plan/deed mismatches. The board voted to approve Form 54 contingent on corrections, approved executive session minutes, and defeated a motion to publicise the abatement window. A resident couple spoke about a large assessment increase on their condo, and the board said it would pursue a state remedy and file the 2025 abatement.

public_comment.topic: Home assessment rose sharply; he and his wife described a disabled husband, a tight budget and a large escrow increase, and asked what the board would do about 2024 and 2025.

The state pays a fixed amount per veteran exemption, reported later in the year; the exact amount was not settled.
A late commitment already approved on November 20.
An invoice for stamps bearing the three assessors' signatures; individual stamps may be ordered later.
Contract for next year's interim valuation; the chair will question the completion deadline.
Two batches of abatements were signed.
Board discussed seeking to restate exemption income thresholds as if the cola had been accepted earlier, requiring warrant work.
A resident said the assessment rose sharply and her escrow raised her mortgage payment.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted by roll call to approve State Tax Form 54 and the FY2025 commitment, contingent on corrections to the form.
A motion to buy newspaper space announcing the abatement deadline failed, with two of the three members voting no.
After a resident couple described a steep condo assessment increase, the board said it would pursue a state remedy and give them an abatement application.
A motion to invite the whole assessor's office staff to the senior center conference failed.
Meetings were set for January 8 and 22, with first and third Wednesdays proposed for February through April.

why_it_matters: Form 54 is the filing behind the FY2025 tax bills, and the board's vote on the public-notice motion leaves the abatement deadline to be learned by word of mouth or the town's existing postings.

A resident who believes an assessment is wrong must file an abatement application before the deadline, so the failed outreach motion and the couple's case show the cost of missing it: escrow-backed payments rise whether or not the assessment is later corrected.
watch_next: Board of Assessors meetings on January 8 and January 22.
The corrected Form 54 signature and the board's follow-up on the couple's property, including the state remedy it said it would pursue.
